old: LLM judges can be useful source-grounding evaluators: the matrix shows strong precision/recall and high passage localization. But evaluations that reuse a model family as both generator and judge should report the full matrix, answer-paired same-vs-cross contrasts, and behavior strata. Apparent false positives should also be adjudicated into induced-error detection, alternate valid error detection, label error, and genuine false alarm. Aggregated same-model metrics are not enough, especially when refusal behavior differs by generator.
addition:
\paragraph{Computational cost.}
With $N$ records and $K$ models in both roles, judging scales as $NK^2$ evaluations, versus $NK$ on the diagonal. Our judge runs recorded 5.63M input and 0.31M output tokens (Appendix~\ref{app:computational-cost}). Frozen answers support an additional judge with $NK$ evaluations.
